questions.subject: accountancy
questions.stem: A firm's capital employed is ₹ 2,50,000 and the normal rate of return is 8%. Each of its two partners is allowed a salary of ₹ 5,000 a year, not yet charged against the profits. Profits were ₹ 41,000 in 2022-23, ₹ 47,000 in 2023-24 and ₹ 50,000 in 2024-25. Goodwill is to be the smaller of two values: (i) 2 years' purchase of the average super profit of all three years; (ii) 3 years' purchase of the average super profit of the last two years. What is the goodwill?
questions.explanation: Partners' salaries are a normal charge, so NCERT adds them to the normal return on capital (deducting them from each year's profit gives the same answer). Normal profit = 2,50,000 × 8% = 20,000, plus salaries 2 × 5,000 = 10,000, so 30,000. If a question gives a market rate of interest instead of a normal rate of return, NCERT (Illustration 13) uses it the same way: interest on capital at that rate, plus the partners' salaries, is the normal profit. Value (i): average profit of the three years = (41,000 + 47,000 + 50,000) ÷ 3 = 46,000; super profit = 46,000 − 30,000 = 16,000; goodwill = 16,000 × 2 = 32,000. Value (ii): average profit of the last two years = (47,000 + 50,000) ÷ 2 = 48,500; super profit = 48,500 − 30,000 = 18,500; goodwill = 18,500 × 3 = 55,500. The smaller value, ₹ 32,000, is the goodwill. Quick route: work with the average profit and take off the normal profit once; there is no need to find each year's super profit. Traps: 55,500 is the larger value; 52,000 leaves the salaries out (super profit 26,000 × 2); 37,000 puts 2 years' purchase on the two-year average (18,500 × 2).
questions.ncert_ref: NCERT Accountancy Part I (leac102), Ch 2 Admission of a Partner, 2.5.4.2 Super Profits Method, p. 60, and Illustration 13, pp. 61-62: partners' salary added to normal profit, goodwill = super profit × years' purchase
